opponent: attention model (move+position one-hot input, Q/K/V self-attention, WINDOW=6)
strategy_summary: Rounds 1-7: the AI plays randomly until it has 7 moves of history, so I played paper every round to give it one clear pattern to learn (3 wins, 2 losses, 2 ties, all luck).

Rounds 8-21: the model had seen little, so I reasoned from what it could have learned. It counters the move it expects, so I played the move that beats that counter, or the move it rated lowest (it almost never plays the counter to a move it thinks unlikely). This went 9 wins, 0 losses, 5 ties.

From round 22 the model began to memorise: it recalled what I had played after the same recent moves, and it reacted to streaks and alternations. I switched to counting my own past follow-ups to the last one or two moves and doing the opposite of what that history predicted. Deliberately repeating scissors when it expected rock after two scissors won three rounds in a row (31-33) before an all-scissors window flipped it.

In the second half it carried a strong scissors bias (scissors was my most frequent move), often 75-99%, so paper won often. Most losses came from pushing a streak one round too long (rounds 34, 38, 40) or from guessing a memorised sequence when the bias won instead (rounds 45, 57).
Late on I favoured moves that could only win or tie against its two likeliest guesses. That kept losses low but produced many ties (the last 10 rounds were 2 wins, 0 losses and 8 ties).

Result: 30 wins, 12 losses, 28 ties. The AI's top expected move matched my actual move in 10 of 63 model rounds (16%), below the 33% of blind guessing. When it was at least 90% confident (17 rounds) it was right 1 times: the model is overconfident, and its confidence is exploitable.

Setup note: this used play_attention.js (the attention model from index.html, with its own state-attention.json), not play.js, which runs the LSTM. Earlier in this session, before the previous attention match, the start of state.json and the first lines of rationale-600.tsv (both from older LSTM matches) were printed by mistake, which PROMPT.md forbids. They were not used here.
